name: Compactness criteria in the complex plane
statement: For a subset of C, compactness is equivalent to sequential compactness and to the open-cover property; in C it is also equivalent to being closed and bounded.
conditions: K is a subset of the complex plane with its Euclidean metric.
conclusion: Any one of the stated compactness conditions implies the others.

Forgetting that a limit must remain in K.
bridge_lemmas: C is complete and finite-dimensional.
Bolzano-Weierstrass gives convergent subsequences of bounded sequences.
repair_templates: State that the setting is C, prove closedness and boundedness, then invoke compactness.

source: Stein and Shakarchi, Complex Analysis.pdf; rewritten seed rule

statement: If Omega is bounded, f is continuous on its closure and holomorphic in Omega, then the maximum of |f| on the closure is attained on the boundary unless f is constant.
